{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox Hurling All-Ireland | year = 1894 | image = | dates = | teams = 5 | connacht = | munster = Cork | leinster = Dublin | ulster = | matches = 4 | poty = | team = Cork | titles = 4th | captain = [[Stephen Hayes (hurler)|Stephen Hayes]] | manager = | team2 = Dublin | captain2 = John McCabe | manager2 = | totalgoals = 15 (3.75 per game) | totalpoints = 53 (13.25 per game) | topscorer = | previous = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1893|1893]] | next = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1895|1895]] }} The '''All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1894''' was the eighth staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier [[inter-county]] [[hurling]] tournament. [[Cork GAA|Cork]] were the [[1893 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champions]].{{cite news|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-41431522.html|title=Blackrock and Dromtariffe recall Phoenix Park days of destiny|publisher=Echo Live|date=15 July 2024|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}}{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport-columnists/arid-41429941.html|title=Paul Rouse: In 1893 All-Ireland final, Cork robbed by Dublin ref: same as it ever was...|publisher=Echo Live|date=5 July 2024|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}} The [[#All-Ireland final|All-Ireland final]] was played at the [[Phoenix Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 24 March 1895 between Cork and [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]], in what was their second meeting in the All-Ireland final overall. Cork won the match by 5–20 to 0–02 to become the first team to win three consecutive titles. It was their fourth All-Ireland title in five years.{{cite news|url=https://hoganstand.com/county/cork/article/index/198271|title=Cork and Dublin bridge 85-year gap|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=7 August 2013|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}}{{cite news|url=https://www.dublingaa.ie/news/recent-meetings-dublin-v-cork-hurling|title=Recent meetings: Dublin v Cork (hurling)|publisher=Dublin GAA website|date=29 July 2021|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}} ==Participating teams== {| class="wikitable" |- !rowspan="2"|County !rowspan="2"|Club !colspan="2"|Most recent success !rowspan="2"| |- !All-Ireland !Provincial |- |[[Cork GAA|Cork]] |[[Blackrock GAA|Blackrock]] |[[1893 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1893]] |[[1893 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1893]] |{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Cork/ClubTitles|title=Club Titles - {{small|(Rapparees)}} |report= |goals1= |goals2= |stadium=[[Phoenix Park]] |attendance=c.2,000 |referee= JJ Kenny (Dublin) }} ==Championship statistics== ===Miscellaneous=== * [[Cork GAA|Cork]]'s 5–20 to 2–00 defeat of [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]], a margin of 29 points, remains the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship records and statistics#Biggest wins|second biggest defeat]] in an All-Ireland final. ==Sources== * Corry, Eoghan, ''The GAA Book of Lists'' (Hodder Headline Ireland, 2005). * Donegan, Des, ''The Complete Handbook of Gaelic Games'' (DBA Publications Limited, 2005). ==References== {{reflist}} {{Hurling All-Irelands}} [[Category:All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championships|1894]] [[Category:1894 in Irish sport]]
